title: Exploring plot styles
text: Setting style = "plain" (default) creates output resembles original “flametree” images: colours vary along body trees, “leaves” drawn.
code: flametree_grow(time = 14) %>%    flametree_plot(     palette = shades,      style = "plain"   ) #> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the flametree package. #>   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/djnavarro/flametree/issues>. #> This warning is displayed once per session. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated.

title: Exploring plot styles
text: Setting style = "voronoi" creates plot tree bodies uniform colour, coloured “leaves” drawn top trees using Voronoi tesselation locations terminal nodes. Note computing tesselation computationally expensive, likely produce errors many nodes.
code: flametree_grow(time = 6, trees = 5) %>%    flametree_plot(     palette = shades,      style = "voronoi"   )

title: Exploring plot styles
text: style = "nativeflora" style creates plot tree bodies rendered thin segments, proportion segments removed, small points drawn end terminal segment.
code: flametree_grow(   time = 10,    trees = 12,    shift_x = spark_nothing() ) %>%    flametree_plot(     palette = shades,      style = "nativeflora"   )

title: Exploring plot styles
text: Setting style = "wisp" similar “nativeflora” style, segments removed, tree body wider base.

title: Exploring plot styles
text: Setting style = "minimal" produces variant use curved segments.
code: flametree_grow(time = 10, trees = 5) %>%    flametree_plot(     palette = shades,      style = "minimal"   )

title: Exploring plot styles
text: Finally, user sets style = "themegray" result plot uses traditional gray theme used ggplot2.
code: flametree_grow(time = 10, trees = 5) %>%    flametree_plot(     palette = shades,      style = "themegray"   )

text: Flametree provides system making generative art R, written two goals mind. First, perhaps foremost, art inherently enjoyable generative artists working R need packages less R users. Second, system designed useful classroom: getting students make artwork class enjoyable exercise flametree can used method introduce key R concepts fun way. can install current version flametree : Alternatively can install development version flametree : Flametree fairly flexible produces art several different styles. One example shown , possibilities described throughout documentation.
code: install.packages("flametree") # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("djnavarro/flametree") library(flametree)  # pick some colours shades <- c("#1b2e3c", "#0c0c1e", "#74112f", "#f3e3e2")  # data structure defining the trees dat <- flametree_grow(time = 10, trees = 10)  # draw the plot dat %>%    flametree_plot(     background = "antiquewhite",     palette = shades,      style = "nativeflora"   ) #> Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0. #> ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead. #> ℹ The deprecated feature was likely used in the flametree package. #>   Please report the issue at <https://github.com/djnavarro/flametree/issues>. #> This warning is displayed once every 8 hours. #> Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was #> generated.

title: Generate the data specifying a flametree — flametree_grow
text: output flametree_grow()` tibble following columns: coord_x, coord_y, id_tree, id_time, id_path, id_leaf, id_pathtree, id_step, seg_deg, seg_len, seg_col, seg_wid. row tibble specifies single point: every curved segment defined three rows. two "coord" columns numeric variables specify location point . "id" columns used indicators various kinds. id_tree column contains numbers specifying tree point belongs , similarly id_time column numeric identifier specifies time point point generated (.e., iteration generative process). id_step column contains number (0, 1, 2) indicating whether point first point, midpoint, end point relevant curved segment tree. addition, two identifier columns used denote segments . id_path column numeric, assigns value 1 "first" segment (.e., lowest part tree trunk) every tree, values increasing numerically subsequent segment. Values id_path uniquely identify segment within tree, multiple trees generated multiple segments id_path value. unique identifier across trees needed, use id_pathtree column, character vector constructed pasting id_path id_tree values string, underscore separator character. addition two coordinate columns six identifier columns, data generated flametree_grow() contains four "seg" columns intended map onto different visual characteristics plot. seg_deg column specifies orientation segment, whereas seg_len denotes length segment, seg_col specifies colour (numeric value interpreted palette), seg_wid specifies width segment. Note information use used differently flametree_plot() function, depending style plot generated.

title: Generate the data specifying a flametree — flametree_grow
text: Generative art created flametree visualisation data structure created calling flametree_grow(). underlying algorithm iterative branching process: tree starts single vertical segment, multiple new segments added end first iteration. multiple iterations creates tree-like structure. user can control iterative process unfolds. setting seed argument random number generator reset using set.seed(). trees argument specifies number trees create using process, time argument specifies many iterations branching process run (least two), split argument specifies many new segments (least two) created time abranching occurs. new segment created, size orientation controlled scale angle arguments. scale argument takes vector least two positive numbers. One numbers selected random whenever new segment created, length new segment equal length "parent" segment created, multiplied scaling factor. orientation new segment controlled angle argument analogous way. Every time new segment generated, one angles (interpreted degrees, radians) selected random. orientation new segment equal orientation parent segment plus sampled angle. Like scale argument, angle must contain least two values. remaining arguments (seg_col, seg_wid, shift_x, shift_y) take functions input, used control colours (seg_col) width (seg_wid) segments created, well horizontal (shift_x) vertical (shift_y) displacement trees generated. Functions passed arguments take four inputs: coord_x, coord_y, id_tree, id_time. function takes variables input can used purpose. However, convenience, four "spark" functions provided can used create functions suitable purpose: spark_linear(), spark_decay(), spark_random(), spark_nothing(). functions documented help files. give example, default behaviour flametree_grow() adds random horizontal displacement tree give impression multiple trees growing side side. suppress horizontal displacement, set shift_x = spark_nothing().

title: Create a plot from a flametree data frame — flametree_plot
text: flametree_plot() function provides several ways visualise data created generative system implemented flametree_grow(). background argument sets background colour image, either string specifying RGB hex colour (e.g., "#000000") colour recognised R (see colours() function details). Analogously, palette argument vector colours. However, palette argument  interpreted slightly differently depending style plot created, discussed . set style resulting plot, pass one following style names: "plain" (default), "voronoi", "wisp", "nativeflora", "minimal", "themegray". Plots "plain" style following properties. Branches trees vary width using seg_wid data column. branch shown curved segment created using geom_bezier2(), colour segments mapped seg_col column data. leaves drawn. style, elements palette used create continuous n-colour gradient using scale_colour_gradientn(). Plots "voronoi" style draw shape tree way plain style, except segments vary colour rendered using geom_bezier() instead geom_bezier2(). Unlike plain style, stylised "leaves" drawn constructing Voronoi tesselation terminal nodes tree. Note computing tesselation computationally expensive likely produce errors many nodes (typically time parameter flametree_grow() large). interpretation palette argument slightly different: first element palette used set colour trees, rest palette colours used create gradient palette used colour tiles depicted Voronoi tesselation. style = "nativeflora" style creates plot tree branches rendered thin segments, proportion segments removed, small points drawn end terminal segment. width branches vary (.e., seg_wid ignored) colour branches constant within tree, vary across trees, ignoring continuous valued seg_col variable using id_tree variable . plain style, palette colours used define n-colour gradient. "wisp" style similar nativeflora, segments removed, wdith branches mapped seg_wid. uses first two elements palette: first element specifies colour branches, second element specifies colour leaf dots. final two styles simplifications styles. "minimal" style similar plain style use curved segments, relying geom_path() draw branches. "themegray" style , ignores palette argument entirely, rendering trees black, set default gray background specified ggplot2 theme_gray() function.

text: arguments flametree_grow() take numeric input, seg_col, seg_wid, shift_x, shift_y take functions input, used control colours (seg_col) width (seg_wid) segments created, well horizontal (shift_x) vertical (shift_y) displacement trees generated. Functions passed arguments take four inputs: coord_x, coord_y, id_tree, id_time input. function takes variables input produces numeric vector length input can used purpose. However, convenience, four "spark" functions provided can used create functions suitable purpose: spark_linear(), spark_decay(), spark_random(), spark_nothing(). Arguments passed one spark functions determine specific function generated. example, spark_linear() can used construct linear combination inputs: spark_linear(x = 3, y = 2) return function computes sum (3 * coord_x) + (2 * coord_y). Different values provided input produce different linear functions. Analogously, spark_decay() returns functions exponentially decaying functions linear combination inputs. spark_random() generator can used generate functions return random values, spark_nothing() produces function always returns zero regardless input.
